items.title: The same element you breathe shields the planet from UV
items.claim: Atmospheric oxygen is O2 — diatomic, vital for respiration. Ozone is O3 — pale blue, pungent, toxic at ground level and protective at altitude. Same element, two molecules, opposite roles.
items.prompt: Why does ozone behave so differently from O2?

options.text: O3's bent three-atom structure with delocalised pi bonding absorbs strongly in the 200-310 nm UV range; O2's MO structure has no comparable visible or near-UV absorption
O3 contains an extra proton per atom

items.reveal:
Ozone is bent with O-O-O angle about 117 degrees and two resonance structures. Its electronic transitions absorb the biologically damaging Hartley UV band.

The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out CFCs to protect the stratospheric ozone layer. It is the most successful environmental treaty by measurable atmospheric impact. The ozone layer is now slowly recovering.

Ground-level ozone produced by photochemical smog damages lungs at parts-per-billion concentrations. Same molecule, life-saving at 30 km, lung-damaging at the surface.
items.why: Allotropes aren't just minor structural variants — they can be biologically and atmospherically opposite.

items.title: The hardest natural material and pencil 'lead' are the same element
items.claim: Diamond scores 10 on the Mohs scale, the maximum. Graphite scores 1-2 — it streaks on paper. Both are 100 percent pure carbon. Identical atoms, opposite mechanical properties.

options.text: Diamond contains stronger isotopes of carbon
Diamond's sp3 carbons form a rigid 3D tetrahedral lattice (all sigma bonds); graphite's sp2 carbons form strong hexagonal sheets held together only by weak dispersion forces, so sheets slide
Diamond is at higher temperature when it forms

items.reveal:
Diamond: every carbon bonded tetrahedrally to four others, all strong sigma bonds. No mobile electrons (insulator), no slip planes (hard).

Graphite: each carbon sp2-hybridised, three in-plane sigma bonds plus a delocalised pi system across the sheet. Sheets stack 0.335 nm apart, held only by van der Waals forces. The pi electrons conduct along the layers; the layers slide past each other — hence the pencil streak.

Thermodynamically, graphite is more stable than diamond by 2.9 kJ/mol at room temperature and pressure. Diamond is metastable; only a kinetic barrier stops it converting to graphite over geological time.
items.why: Element identity isn't enough — bonding arrangement (allotropy) can transform a substance utterly.

items.title: Two molecules with identical formulas, opposite effects
items.claim: Thalidomide was sold in the 1950s as a sedative and anti-nausea drug for pregnant women. The molecule has a single chiral centre. One enantiomer treats morning sickness. The other causes catastrophic birth defects.
items.prompt: Why couldn't doctors simply sell the 'safe' enantiomer?

options.text: The safe enantiomer is too expensive to purify
Thalidomide racemises in the body — even if you give pure (R)-thalidomide, the body converts some to the harmful (S) form
Doctors did sell the safe one — the thalidomide disaster never actually happened

items.reveal:
Receptors in the body are chiral. They distinguish enantiomers the way a left hand distinguishes a left glove from a right glove. The (R) enantiomer of thalidomide sedates; the (S) enantiomer binds to a different protein involved in limb development.

The critical complication: thalidomide racemises in vivo. The chiral centre is alpha to a carbonyl, and the proton there can be lost and re-added on either face. So even pure (R)-thalidomide becomes a racemic mixture inside the body within hours.

Modern pharma uses chiral synthesis and tests both enantiomers for activity AND for unintended effects.
items.why: Two molecules with the same atoms in the same order can behave like medicine and poison. Stereochemistry is consequential.
